_comment: This file holds what JJ Flexible says and shows, for the settings area. Settings and per-radio configuration. EDITING: change the text on the right of the colon; never change the key on the left, and never change anything inside curly braces such as {radio} - those are filled in at run time with the actual radio name, frequency and so on. A key whose text is missing is spoken as the key itself, so if you hear something like connect.radio_found read out literally, that key needs text. YOUR OWN COPY: put a file of this same name in the lexicon folder beside your settings and it layers on top of this one, key by key - you only need the keys you want to change, and everything else keeps working. If your file has a typo in it, it is ignored and this one is used, so a mistake can never stop the program. LADDERS: a key may hold three tiers instead of one string - critical, terse and chatty - which is how one message gets shorter as you turn verbosity down. This partition is empty; the extraction tracks fill it. See docs/planning/active/string-store-contract.md.

settings.audio.pc_audio_on_remote: On. Radio audio is playing through this computer, which on a remote connection is the only way to hear it.

settings.path_learning.cleared: Cleared the connection history for {cleared} radio{plural}. Learning starts again from the next connection.
settings.path_learning.cleared_with_fail: Cleared the connection history for {cleared} radio{plural}. {failed} could not be cleared — your trace file has the reason, and those radios may still follow their old habit.
settings.path_learning.forget_body: JJ Flexible works out a radio's usual connection path by reading that radio's own connection history. There is nowhere else it is written down, so forgetting what was learned means clearing that history.
settings.path_learning.forget_question: Clear the connection history for every radio?
settings.path_learning.forget_warning_ch: Connection paths you chose yourself are NOT touched. Only what JJ Flexible worked out on its own goes away.
settings.path_learning.forget_warning_hi: Every radio this computer knows loses its record of the last ten connection attempts: which way each one went, whether it worked, and how long it took.
settings.path_learning.forget_warning_re: It starts learning again from the next connection.
settings.path_learning.forget_warning_su: That record is also what answers 'how long is my connect actually taking', so a support conversation about a slow connection starts from nothing again.
settings.path_learning.not_written: {what} This could not be written to disk, so it may not be here next time you start. Your trace file has the reason.
settings.path_learning.nothing_to_clear: There was no connection history to clear.
settings.path_learning.status_off: Off. Nothing is prefilled from history, and the number of connects is not used, so it is switched off above. Connection paths you chose yourself are unaffected; radios without a choice try the local network first.
settings.path_learning.status_on: On. A radio has to connect the same way {threshold} times running before JJ Flexible tries that way first, and only for radios you have not already chosen a path for.
settings.path_learning.threshold_set: {wanted} connects in a row before JJ Flexible tries a radio's usual path first.
settings.path_learning.turned_off: Learning the connection path is off. Nothing will be prefilled from history. Paths you chose yourself are unaffected.
settings.path_learning.turned_on: Learning the connection path is on, after {threshold} connects in a row the same way.

settings.updates.up_to_date: You're up to date on the {channel} channel.
